claim: Same-origin hosting of UI and BFF means the auth cookie is sent automatically and no CORS headers are required; split-host requires credentials:include plus CORS.
quote: requests from the front end to the backend will automatically include the authentication cookie and not require CORS headers

claim: A BFF requires transforming downstream OpenAPI specs: rewrite paths to the BFF prefix, rewrite servers to the BFF host, merge multiple downstream docs, strip security schemes, and add an X-CSRF request interceptor so Swagger UI works with the BFF cookie.
quote: The server URLs in these documents represent the direct URL to the API. Clients shouldn't access the API directly but through the BFF.

claim: MapRemoteBffApiEndpoint maps a local BFF path onto a remote API address and forwards all sub-paths; all such endpoints require an x-csrf header, which triggers a CORS preflight for cross-origin calls.
quote: app.MapRemoteBffApiEndpoint("/api/users", new Uri("https://remoteHost/users")).WithAccessToken(RequiredTokenType.User);

claim: The /bff/user endpoint returns the session claims plus bff:logout_url, bff:session_expires_in and bff:session_state; returns 401 when anonymous; requires the X-CSRF: 1 header. Management endpoints sit under a configurable ManagementBasePath (default /bff).
quote: returns data about the currently logged-on user and the session

claim: Duende ships official BFF samples for OpenAPI, YARP integration, and Separate Host for UI (which covers AllowedOrigins, CORS policy and cookie SameSite settings for split-host dev).
quote: configure AllowedOrigins, CORS policy, and cookie SameSite settings for split-host development and production deployments

claim: A 'site' is scheme + eTLD+1; the port is not part of the site definition. So localhost:5173 and localhost:5000 on the same scheme are same-site, but http://localhost and https://localhost are cross-site (schemeful same-site).
quote: Websites that have the same scheme and the same eTLD+1 are considered "same-site".

claim: Vite server.proxy supports target, changeOrigin, secure, ws and rewrite. Reverse proxies in front of Vite must proxy WebSocket, else the HMR client falls back to connecting directly to the Vite HMR server.
quote: reverse proxies in front of Vite are expected to support proxying WebSocket ... the client will fall back to connecting the WebSocket directly to the Vite HMR server bypassing the reverse proxies

claim: A working standalone Duende BFF + Vite dev setup runs two processes (BFF on https://localhost:7164, Vite on https://localhost:4378) and proxies four route groups from Vite to the BFF: /bff, /api, /signin-oidc, /signout-callback-oidc, with secure:false for the self-signed cert; @vitejs/plugin-basic-ssl provides Vite HTTPS.
quote: outside of your local dev environment, you'll need to deploy a reverse proxy

claim: .NET 10 Microsoft.AspNetCore.OpenApi defaults to OpenAPI 3.1, supports YAML output via a .yaml/.yml suffix on MapOpenApi (but not at build time), supports build-time generation via Microsoft.Extensions.ApiDescription.Server / GetDocument.Insider, and exposes a ShouldInclude delegate.
quote: Generating OpenAPI documents in YAML format at build time isn't supported but planned for a future preview.

claim: Document, operation and schema transformers ship in .NET 10; document transformers have access to the entire OpenAPI document and can mutate it (e.g. Info, Components.SecuritySchemes, Paths). .NET 10 adds GetOrCreateSchemaAsync and Document.AddComponent inside transformers.
quote: Document transformers have access to the entire OpenAPI document. These can be used to make global modifications to the document.

claim: Swagger UI cannot exercise cookie-authenticated endpoints via 'Try it out'.
quote: Cookie authentication is currently not supported for "try it out" requests due to browser security restrictions.

claim: Swagger UI is architected as a public client that injects bearer tokens and bypasses cookies/CSRF, which a secure BFF rejects; a Swagger UI plugin can route calls through the BFF, add CSRF headers, and be served same-origin.
quote: expects to inject Bearer tokens into headers (which a secure BFF should reject)

claim: Kiota's TypeScript client has no built-in way to configure fetch options, so setting credentials:'include' for a cookie BFF requires hand-writing a custom fetch function.
quote: Fetch has a native option to include secure cookies in requests, but Kiota doesn't provide a way to configure fetch options out of the box when creating the client.

claim: Kiota provides an AnonymousAuthenticationProvider that performs no operation, for APIs that don't require a token — the natural choice under a cookie BFF.
quote: For APIs that don't require authentication, the abstractions packages provide an AnonymousAuthenticationProvider, which serves as a placeholder and performs no operation.

claim: openapi-fetch's createClient accepts baseUrl plus any valid fetch option, so cookie auth under a BFF is a two-line change (baseUrl + credentials:'include').
quote: Any valid fetch option (headers, mode, cache, signal …)

claim: NSwag's WithCredentials = true setting does not emit credentials into the generated Fetch-template TypeScript client — an open issue; use transformOptions instead.
quote: Adding WithCredentials = true to TypeScriptClientGeneratorSettings isn't changing the generated Typescript client

claim: NSwag exposes UseTransformOptionsMethod, which requires implementing a transformOptions method that receives and returns the RequestInit options — the hook for credentials:'include' and the X-CSRF header.
quote: The required "transformOptions" method can be implemented per client class or as a base class for all clients

claim: Orval supports an output baseUrl and an override.mutator custom fetch/axios instance, which is where cookie credentials and the CSRF header go.
quote: baseUrl allows you to add a part of the url that's been omitted from the specification or set the entire server url as a prefix for all operations.

claim: Hey API's fetch client createClient accepts baseUrl, headers and credentials, so cookie auth under a BFF is configuration, not code generation changes.
quote: createClient configuration supports baseUrl, headers, credentials and other fetch options

claim: Aspire's AddViteApp puts the Vite dev server in the app model, injects the API address as a services__* env var that vite.config.js reads to build server.proxy, orchestrates Keycloak as a container, and starts everything with one command plus a unified dashboard.
quote: This eliminates CORS issues during development by proxying requests through the same origin.

claim: Aspire 13.2 (March 2026) closed 1,100+ issues, themed on the CLI as a first-class agent interface, a TypeScript AppHost preview, and seamless local development.
quote: .NET Aspire 13.2 Released with Expanded CLI, TypeScript AppHost Preview, and Dashboard Improvements

claim: Aspire pays off with multiple communicating services and complex local setup, but adds unnecessary overhead for a single API plus a database; its local dev experience is more polished than its deployment story as of 2026.
quote: for single-API projects with just a database, Aspire adds unnecessary overhead, and a standard ASP.NET Core template is simpler and faster to work with

claim: YARP itself has no built-in OpenAPI aggregation; a small third-party extension reuses YARP cluster/route config to publish an aggregated Swagger document.
quote: It's an easy to use Swagger extension for the YARP project.

claim: Browsers increasingly block third-party cookies, and cookies are blocked during navigation between different sites — so SameSite=None is not a safe workaround for split-host dev.
quote: If the BFF and OpenID Connect Provider (OP) are hosted on different sites, then some browsers will block cookies from being sent during navigation between those sites.

claim: vite-plugin-mkcert generates a locally-trusted CA and certificates for Vite's HTTPS dev server, one option for matching the .NET HTTPS dev scheme.
quote: Provide certificates for vite's https dev service.

claim: The ASP.NET Core dev certificate can be exported as a PFX and fed to Vite so both dev servers share the HTTPS scheme.
quote: dotnet dev-certs https -ep "C:\User\me\localhost.pfx" -p "dummypass"

claim: The Aspire Q1 2026 roadmap update confirms active investment in the CLI, TypeScript AppHost and local development experience.
quote: Aspire Roadmap - Q1 2026 Update (March 2026)
